page: Microsoft Azure F1als_v7 is a single-core virtual machine belonging to the Falsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server is configured with 1 vCPU, 1 physical core, and 1 thread per core. It includes 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Due to its single-core architecture, the stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all rank in the top tier. However, multi-core stress-ng performance and the overall PassMark CPU score fall into the weak category. Memory performance is also constrained; the PassMark memory score is in the poor category, and small-block read-only memory bandwidth is weak, though large-block read and write bandwidths maintain average tier performance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F1als_v7 offers a low-resource entry point with high-frequency dedicated compute, making it suitable for workloads that require strong single-threaded execution without massive memory overhead. It is appropriate for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic utility scripting, simple web serving, or small-scale LLM inference with tiny models, where multi-threaded scaling and large memory footprints are not required.
